name: SANKET all-factor confidence
algorithm: Gradient-boosted trees (scikit-learn HistGradientBoosting, monotone in rain and soil moisture), isotonic calibration

feature_labels.prior_landslides_10km: Earlier NASA landslide records within 10 km

training_data.positives_description: India, rainfall-triggered, dated: NASA Global Landslide Catalog 2007-2016 and NASA COOLR reports (location accuracy <= 5 km), Kerala 2018 monsoon inventory (Univ. Twente / GSI, DANS, CC-BY-4.0) and NASA COOLR Himachal July 2023 inventory, thinned to one point per ~5 km cell
training_data.negatives: same place on 3 other days without a catalogued landslide (25 km / 7 days), and 1 random point in India on the same day
training_data.weather: ERA5 via Open-Meteo through the day before each dated case. Both live feeds use the same 3–240 hour rainfall windows and 3-hour temperature and wind sampling.
training_data.terrain: Copernicus elevation, relief and gradient over ~550 m. Training uses GLO-90. Live uses bundled GLO-90 hotspot stencils or the equivalent GLO-30 stencil.
training_data.vegetation: NASA Terra MODIS via GIBS (2004–2006 vegetation baseline). Mean of available quarterly samples in 2004–2006, estimated from the official NDVI color bins, at about 2 km resolution.
training_data.landslide_history: NASA Global Landslide Catalog and COOLR reports. Dated events within 10 km, at least 30 days before the scored date. Zero means no matching catalogue record.

meaning_of_confidence: Calibrated probability that a landslide is recorded within ~5 km on that day, for cases mixed like the training set (1 landslide day per 4 non-landslide days). Real landslide days are far rarer, so read it as a relative alarm level and use the validated hit / false-alarm table.
limitations: The catalogue is news-based: remote landslides are under-reported, so some negatives are really landslide days.
ERA5 (~25 km) underestimates local cloudbursts; some events had little ERA5 rain.
Locations are accurate to ~1-5 km, so terrain is described at ~0.5 km scale, not the exact slope.
Events after 2018 are sparse in public catalogues; Kerala 2018 events are dated to the 16 Aug peak (exact day unknown).
Vegetation is a fixed pre-training baseline. It cannot capture recent changes such as deforestation.
Nearby landslide counts depend on catalogue coverage, record dates, and location accuracy.
Weather is cut off before the case date because the event hour is generally unknown. This evaluation measures discrimination between catalogue cases and sample controls.
